ai.definition: Onshore wind technology involves the installation of wind turbines on land to harness the kinetic energy from the wind and convert it into electricity.
ai.howItWorks: Wind turbines consist of large blades connected to a generator. When wind blows, it turns the blades which spin a shaft in a generator, producing electrical power. This process is managed by advanced control systems that optimize performance based on wind conditions.
ai.problemSolved: Reduces reliance on fossil fuels and decreases greenhouse gas emissions, contributing to global efforts against climate change.
ai.manufacturing: Components are mass-produced with standardized designs; assembly involves precise fitting of blades, tower sections, and nacelles (enclosures housing the generator).
ai.buildProcess: Site selection is crucial considering wind speed, topography, and environmental impact. Turbines are transported to site via road or rail, then assembled on a concrete foundation.
ai.costDrivers: Initial investment costs due to large-scale infrastructure; operational expenses related to maintenance and grid integration.
ai.lifecycleOutlook: continuing growth in adoption as part of renewable energy portfolios.
ai.regulation: Varies by country, often involving permits for land use and environmental assessments. Some regions offer incentives like tax credits or feed-in tariffs to promote installation.
ai.risks: Weather-related downtime; potential for blade damage from storms; visual and noise pollution concerns leading to community opposition.
ai.profitability: High in areas with consistent wind patterns, benefiting from decreasing costs of technology and increasing demand for clean energy.
ai.futureDevelopment: Focus on larger turbine designs, higher efficiency, and integration with smart grid technologies. Offshore wind is also expanding as a complementary renewable resource.

glossary.def: The energy possessed by an object due to its motion.
A mechanical device that transfers rotational speed and torque between two shafts, often used in wind turbines to increase the generator's speed from the slower turbine rotation.
The housing of a wind turbine's electrical and mechanical components, including the generator and gearbox.

subsystems.name: Rotor
subsystems.role: captures kinetic energy from the wind and turns it into rotation.
parts: composite blades (glass fibre, sometimes carbon fibre in the spar)

subsystems.name: Drivetrain and nacelle
subsystems.role: converts slow, high-torque rotation into grid-frequency electricity.

subsystems.name: Tower and foundation
subsystems.role: holds the rotor high in smoother wind and transfers loads to the ground.

subsystems.name: Electrical collection and grid connection
subsystems.role: gathers power from every turbine and delivers it to the transmission network.

subsystems.name: Control and monitoring
subsystems.role: keeps the turbine pointed at the wind, limits loads and reports performance.

subsystems.name: Installation and maintenance equipment
subsystems.role: the cranes, trucks and service crews that build and sustain a wind farm.

buildSteps.title: Measure the wind and study the site
buildSteps.detail: Met masts or ground-based LiDAR record wind speed and direction for at least a year; engineers check access roads, grid capacity and environmental constraints.

buildSteps.title: Prepare roads and foundations
buildSteps.detail: Access tracks are built and reinforced concrete foundations are poured, with anchor bolts set to hold the tower base.

buildSteps.title: Fabricate the tower
buildSteps.detail: Steel plate is rolled into conical sections, welded, painted and shipped to site in transportable lengths.

buildSteps.title: Make the blades
buildSteps.detail: Fibre mats are laid in large moulds, infused with resin and cured; the two shell halves are bonded around a spar to form a stiff, light blade.

buildSteps.title: Assemble the nacelle
buildSteps.detail: Gearbox or direct-drive generator, shaft, converter and control panels are assembled and tested in a factory before shipping.

buildSteps.title: Erect the turbine
buildSteps.detail: A crane lifts tower sections into place, then the nacelle, then the blades — either as a pre-assembled rotor or one at a time.

buildSteps.title: Connect and commission
buildSteps.detail: Collector cables are buried, the project substation is energised, and each turbine is tested until it can export power reliably.

buildSteps.title: Operate and maintain
buildSteps.detail: Scheduled inspections, oil changes and blade repairs keep the farm running for its 20–30 year design life.

prerequisites.why: light, strong blades are what make large rotors practical.
converters must keep voltage and frequency stable as wind varies.
towers and nacelles weighing many tonnes must be lifted and moved to inland sites.
a project is only economic if the long-term wind is well understood before construction.

pathway.milestone: onshore wind is a mature, widely deployed source of low-cost electricity
pathway.unlocks: displacing fossil generation on many grids.

pathway.milestone: larger rotors on taller towers and repowering of older sites
pathway.unlocks: more energy from the same land and grid connection.

pathway.milestone: co-location with batteries and smarter grid controls
pathway.unlocks: smoother output and better use of existing transmission.

pathway.milestone: recyclable blades and circular supply chains
pathway.unlocks: reduced waste and a fully sustainable lifecycle.
